title: Even and Odd Functions and Inverse Functions
seo_title: Precalculus Even, Odd and Inverse Functions Worksheets (TEKS P.2D, P.2E)
standard_text: P.2D describe symmetry of graphs of even and odd functions; P.2E determine an inverse function, when it exists, for a given function over its domain or a subset of its domain and represent the inverse using multiple representations
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets for Texas TEKS P.2D and P.2E: even and odd functions, symmetry, inverse functions from equations and tables, and checking inverses. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: An inverse exists when no output repeats.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Even: f(−x) = f(x). The graph is symmetric about the y-axis.
  • Odd: f(−x) = −f(x). The graph is symmetric about the origin.
  • A polynomial with only even powers (and a constant) is even; with only odd powers it is odd.
  • An inverse function exists when f is one-to-one. Swap x and y and solve for y. Check with f(f−1(x)) = x.

Examples

Example

f(x) = x3 − 4x

f(−x) = −x3 + 4x = −f(x)

Answer: Odd

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Odd because of one odd powerx3 + 2 is neither: the constant is an even power.
Mixing up the symmetriesEven: y-axis. Odd: origin.
Reading f−1 as 1/ff−1 is the inverse function.

sets.title: Find the inverse of a function

items.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = x + 35.
items.e: Swap: x = y + 35. Multiply by 5: 5x = y + 3. Then subtract 3: f−1(x) = 5x − 3.

items.q: Find the inverse of f(x) = x + 55.
items.e: Swap: x = y + 55. Multiply by 5: 5x = y + 5. Then subtract 5: f−1(x) = 5x − 5.
Swap: x = √(y − 2). Square: x² = y − 2, so y = x² + 2. The outputs of f are ≥ 0, so the inverse uses x ≥ 0. f−1(x) = x² + 2, for x ≥ 0.
Swap x and y, then undo in reverse order: add 6, then take the cube root. f−1(x) = ∛(x + 6).
Swap x and y, then undo in reverse order: add 7, divide by 2, then take the cube root. f−1(x) = ∛(x + 72).
Swap x and y, then undo in reverse order: subtract 2, divide by 3, then take the cube root. f−1(x) = ∛(x − 23).
Swap x and y: x = 5y + 7. Solve for y: subtract 7, then divide by 5. f−1(x) = x − 75. (The reciprocal 1/f(x) is not the inverse.)
Swap x and y: x = 4y − 4. Solve for y: subtract −4, then divide by 4. f−1(x) = x + 44. (The reciprocal 1/f(x) is not the inverse.)
